passage: Confidential note from Madhuri, member of the workplace committee. Vandana came to see me on Tuesday, unsure whether what she had experienced was "serious enough." She said a senior colleague had been commenting on her appearance, and once put a hand on her shoulder after she had told him to stop. She had not reported it because she doubted herself. I told her it is serious, that it is not her fault, and that she did not need a name for it to be allowed to speak. Together we wrote down the dates and what was said. She then told the colleague, in writing, that the comments must stop. I explained the committee's steps, and she chose to file a formal complaint that same day. I checked in with her on Thursday and again a week later.

qa.q: What did Vandana tell the colleague in writing?
qa.a: She told him that the comments must stop.

qa.q: Why had Vandana not reported it earlier?
qa.a: She doubted herself and wondered whether it was serious enough.

qa.q: What did Madhuri do after listening to Vandana?
qa.a: Madhuri said it was serious and not her fault, wrote down the dates and words with her, explained the committee's steps and checked in later.

qa.q: How might Vandana have felt on hearing that it was serious?
qa.a: She may have felt relieved to be believed, though possibly still nervous about filing.

grounding: A committee member's note shows a colleague's unwanted remarks and touch being taken seriously, with a clear no, written details and use of the committee.
